qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Branch density and core commercial/retail deposit relationships create modest switching friction, but banking products are commoditized. Multi-cycle ROIC of 5-8% (10Y median 7.8%) and ROTCE of 10-11% fail the 12% GAAP / 15% tangible hurdle. Zero pricing power above inflation due to deposit beta pressures, SOFR-linked asset repricing, and fierce competition from money-center banks and fintechs.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Regional bank with commoditized retail and commercial banking offerings. Multi-cycle ROIC of ~5-8% (10Y median 7.8%) and ROTCE of 10-11% fall far short of the 12% GAAP / 15% tangible return hurdles. Zero pricing power over inflation against national money-center banks and digital competitors.
qualitative.evidence: Citizens Financial Group (CFG) operates ~$226B in total assets and ~$183B in deposits (FY2025) with net interest margins of 2.87%-3.07%. Profitability remains structurally below compounder thresholds: FY2023-2025 GAAP ROE was 6.2%-7.2%, GAAP ROTCE 9.8%-10.9% (underlying ROTCE 10.5%-13.5%), and ROIC 4.6%-6.1% (10Y median 7.8%), failing the 12% GAAP ROIC / 15% ROTCE proof-of-moat test. Core deposit accounts provide modest switching friction, but pricing is strictly market-dictated by SOFR benchmarks, deposit betas, and competition from national giants (JPMorgan, BofA) and money market funds. Inherent fractional-reserve duration risk reinforces sub-hurdle status (g6_default N).
